subject: Request: pricing floor exception for reserved capacity linked to GPU index
messages:
From: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@orchardhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orchard Health Procurement <procurement@orchardhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity pricing question and GPU index pass-through

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers look promising. Procurement asked me to reach out on one open item before we go to legal: Orchard is asking for a limited pricing floor / discount protection tied to GPU market moves for a 24-month reserved capacity commit. Their ask: a 10% one-time discount now (applied to committed unit price) plus a 2-way pass-through if spot GPU pricing moves more than 20% during the term.

Key context from Orchard: their workload is latency-sensitive triage and embeddings at scale; they expect steady growth from 50M to 120M tokens/month over year one. They need predictability for budgeting.

Can Redwood support a pilot structure like that, or do you need an alternative proposal (e.g., graduated discount linked to committed tiers, or a GPU-index cap)? Also, can you share a short version of the capacity profile they should include in their SOW?

Attaching a draft capacity profile they created for reference (orchard_capacity_profile.xlsx).

Thanks,
Ethan

--
Ethan Morales

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity pricing question and GPU index pass-through

Ethan —

Really appreciate the clarity. We can do something that balances Orchard's budget certainty with Redwood's exposure to GPU market swings. Two quick asks so I can route this internally:

1) Can you confirm the committed monthly token baseline you want Redwood to reserve for month 1 and the growth ramp (if different from the attached)?
2) Would Orchard consider a 24-month commit with a 6–12 month stepped ramp instead of a flat 24-month baseline? That helps us price the discount.

What I can propose now (subject to finance + leadership approval):
- Provisional 10% one-time commit discount applied to the committed unit price at signature.
- A GPU-index trigger: if Redwood's weighted GPU spot index moves >20% up from current average, Orchard would pay an index pass-through that reduces the discount proportionally; if the index drops >20%, Redwood would offer a rebate to Orchard.
- Cap: finance to propose a maximum pass-through floor (we'll surface scenarios).

I'll loop in finance and sales leadership and share a quick scenario workbook. Attached: a short capacity profile template for the SOW and our initial ask list (orchard_capacity_profile.xlsx).

If Orchard can sign off on the ramp numbers today, I can escalate for expedited review.

Thanks —
Kimberly

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity pricing question and GPU index pass-through — requesting quick finance review

Team — forward below (from Orchard). They want a 24-month reserve with a 10% upfront commit discount and a two-way GPU index pass-through if market moves >20%.

Why this matters: if we grant a one-time 10% discount plus a pass-through, our unit economics can deteriorate materially if GPU prices spike. But Orchard is a high-probability close and strategic (long-term healthcare account).

Request: can finance run 3 scenarios and advise an approved structure we can offer without exec signoff vs. one that requires leadership sign-off? I've attached a quick workbook with inputs (gpu-index-scenario.xlsx) and Orchard's profile.

- Scenario A (conservative): approval delegated to finance — 8% max discount, pass-through limited to +/-12% with cap.
- Scenario B (middle): requires head-of-sales approval — 10% discount, pass-through +/-20% with reimbursement floor.
- Scenario C (stretch): requires CFO/CEO sign-off — 12% discount, pass-through unlimited (redwood carries spike risk).

Please reply with recommended path and any contract language we should require (e.g., minimum token baseline, ramp schedule, audit right for GPU index proof).

Thanks — urgent where possible.

Kim

[Attached: gpu-index-scenario.xlsx, orchard_capacity_profile.xlsx]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity pricing question and GPU index pass-through — finance scenarios

Kim —

Quick finance read on the attached workbook (gpu-index-scenario.xlsx). I modeled current exchange-weighted GPU spot index and three shock cases: +25% spike, -30% drop, and sustained +15% drift. Summary below (net to Redwood margin on committed units):

- Scenario A (8% discount cap, +/-12% pass-through cap): expected margin drop ~3.6% in +25% shock, worst-case ~6.8% over 24 months if spikes persist.
- Scenario B (10% discount, +/-20%): expected margin drop ~5.1% in +25% shock, worst-case ~9.8% sustained.
- Scenario C (12% discount, unlimited pass-through): severe exposure — could exceed 12% margin erosion in prolonged stress.

Recommendation: approve Scenario B as the customer-facing offer only if leadership signs off to hold reserve for strategic accounts and we include the following mitigations in contract:

1) Annual true-up with an agreed GPU index (third-party published index or our weighted internal index) and audit rights for index calculation.
2) Cap pass-through for any single quarter to 8% of monthly invoice to protect cashflow spikes.
3) Minimum committed baseline (month 1) and step-ramp schedule (months 7 and 13).
4) Early termination clause with buyout if Orchard materially under-utilizes (>40% below baseline for two consecutive quarters).

If leadership prefers not to sign off, we can offer Scenario A without executive approval. Scenario A reduces exposure but may jeopardize the economic ask for Orchard.

I've attached the workbook with the modeled numbers and a sample contract snippet we can hand to legal (see tab 'contract_snippet').

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Finance — Pricing & Capacity
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity pricing question and GPU index pass-through — finance scenarios

Thanks team — I've reviewed Rishi's scenarios. Orchard is strategic for our healthcare vertical and the deal velocity is high. I'm willing to authorize a provisional exception with conditions.

Authorization (provisional, pending final SOW & legal review):
- Approve Scenario B structure: 10% one-time commit discount for a 24-month reserved commit with step-ramp schedule.
- Pass-through: two-way GPU-index adjustment with a +/-20% trigger, BUT cap any single monthly pass-through to 8% of that month's invoice.
- Require the following contract items before signature: explicit GPU index definition & calculation method, quarterly true-up with audit right, minimum baseline and ramp schedule, and a 6-month buyout schedule if materially under-utilized.
- Finance to own the periodic true-up mechanics; Legal to draft the clause.

Kim — please finalize the MOP/SOW (attach orchard_mop_draft.pdf) and send to Ethan with the provisional terms. If Orchid (sic) signs otherwise, escalate to me. I want the final docs in my inbox before we route to Legal.

Vivek
